problem:
The random variable $X$ has the following probability distribution.

| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{X}(x)$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.5$ |

Let $Y={X}^{4}.$ The distribution of $Y$ is given below.

| $y$ | $0$ | $a$ | $b$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $c$ | $0.2$ | $d$ |

What is the value of $a+b+d?$

feedback.problem:
The random variable $X$ has the following probability distribution.

| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{X}(x)$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.4$ |

Let $Y={X}^{2}.$ The distribution of $Y$ is given below.

| $y$ | $0$ | $1$ | $a$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.1$ | $b$ | $c$ |

What is the value of $a+c?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's add a $Y={X}^{2}$ row to our table.

| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $4$ | $1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $4$ |
| ${f}_{X}(x)$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.4$ |

$$

$$

From the table, we see that $Y\in {0,1,4}.$ Notice that we now have two columns for both $Y=1$ and $Y=4.$

We calculate the probabilities associated with each value of $Y$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y=0) & =0.1 \\ P(Y=1) & =0.1+0.2 \\ P(Y=4) & =0.2+0.4\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the following table.

| $y$ | $0$ | $1$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ | $0.6$ |

Therefore, $a=4,b=0.3,c=0.6,$ and $a+c=4.6.$
